thread.title: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) uses $163 billion to dampen Wall Street’s disappointment over sales

author: Ram Shaw
title: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) uses $163 billion to dampen Wall Street’s disappointment over sales
text:
February 4, 2018 Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) uses $163 billion to dampen Wall Street’s disappointment over sales 
Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) is going to use the sheer power of its huge cash holdings in a bid to stifle Wall Street’s disappointment regarding its iPhone sales. 
On Thursday, the smartphone manufacturer released lower than expected fourth quarter iPhone unit sales. The company also provided a weaker than expected revenue estimate for the March quarter. The company’s stock has declined by 4.4 percent on Friday. 
The company also announced a target to use about all of its $163 billion in net cash, suggesting more stock buybacks, acquisitions or dividends. In the December quarter, its total cash holdings increased to $285 billion, however, its total debt was $122 billion. 
Previously, the company has announced plans to make about $38 billion in tax payments to the US government under the new tax strategy’s repatriation rate for its cumulative foreign earnings. 
Luca Maestri, Chief Financial Officer said on the earnings call on Thursday that tax reform would allow them to follow a more optimal capital structure for their company. Their current net cash position is $163 billion and they are targeting to become around net cash neutral over time, given the higher financial and operational flexibility from the access to their foreign cash. 
The executive noted that during the past several years, the company has returned about 100 percent of its free cash flow to investors.   taking that approach while being very thoughtful and deliberate about it. He added that the company would not make any modifications to its mergers and acquisition strategy, while it would continue to look “at all sizes” and projected to accelerate their product road maps through its acquisitions. 
CEO Tim Cook explained that the company’s cash position will not get hurt literally. He said what Luca’s argued is not cash equivalent to zero, rather he meant there is an equal amount of cash and debt and that they equate to zero. 
Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) said it would disclose details of the new capital allocation plan when it will release its March quarter earnings report. About Ram Shaw
